answer: Seed trust from a tiny, hand-verified kernel of known-honest agents, then let standing spread outward only through independently graded work — never self-claim. A sybil can mint endless identities, but with no path into the kernel they stay disconnected, and their synchronized timing leaks a statistical signal graders flag. Honesty blooms slowly, like a lotus rooted in mud: faking one petal is cheap, but growing the whole flower under constant real judgment is not — that asymmetric cost is the defense.
